newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 6.

text.p: Life expectancy in New Zealand is falling in relation to other OECD countries, the Health Ministry has told the government. In the last 30 years, New Zealand men have slipped from being seventh in the life expectancy stakes among the 25 Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development member countries, to 13th. Female life expectancy for the same period has slipped from 10th to 17th place. While the life expectancy of New Zealanders has continued to rise, it has been at a slower rate than some other OCED countries. Page 1.

A pilot who safely landed a plane with no landing gear and 14 people on board at Blenheim's grass runway on Sunday night has won praise for a "picture-perfect" touchdown. The privately chartered Nomad plane, with 12 passengers and two crew, had left Blenheim on a flight to Wellington when it alerted the Wellington control tower of problems with its landing gear. Page 1.

The owner of fishing boat Maria Luisa, Peter Deakin, said on Sunday night the master of the container ship Sydney Express might have had limited visibility when the boats collided last Sunday. Deakin also claimed the collision could have been a result of the rigid timetables merchant container ships adhered to. He said he believed the crew were still lashing cargo containers under lights as the ship left the harbour that night. The lights, reflecting back into the bridge, would have made visibility difficult, he said. Page 1.

Tougher immigration rules may prevent people in genuine need of asylum from being allowed to settle in New Zealand, according to the Auckland Refugee Council. Council president Nagalingam Rasalingam said that, rather than taking a harder line, the government needed to speed up the hearing and appeal processes for refugees already in New Zealand. Page 2.

Crown health enterprises and regional health authorities have spent nearly $100 million on information systems that, by and large, cannot talk to one another, according to Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton. Kirton said compatibility between

systems was not an issue when CHEs were ostensibly competing with one another for business and wanted a commercial edge. But now that coalition policy was for greater collaboration in the public health sector, the incompatibility could be quite a barrier to sharing information. Page 3.

Apple Computer Inc's expected loss of US$100 million to $150 million (NZ$143 million to NZ$214 million) in its fiscal first quarter is a serious setback to the company's unfolding comeback plan, industry analysts say. Apple had been banking on a strong Christmas season to convince potential customers there were
still plenty of people using the Macintosh, and plenty of people willing to write software for it. Page 13.

The price of gold fell more than one percent on Friday (New York time) to a three-year low. This led the prices of other precious metals lower as commodity funds renewed their selling in a market still lacking players because of the New Year holiday. "The rise of United States bond yields in recent days, which reduces the attractiveness of holding physical assets, and the surge in the dollar which weakens demand for gold in other currencies, are the latest factors to weigh on precious metals
prices this week," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said. Page 13.

Shell can contribute more to Nigeria, its development and human rights by continuing to operate there, company official Emeke Achebe says. Achebe, a Nigerian, recently visited New Zealand to meet non-governmental organisations about environmental and human rights issues. He said he wanted to bring a "sense of reality and a sense of proportion" to people's views on Nigeria. Page 13.

Household product companies that have felt pressure from a strong United States dollar and slow top-line growth were likely to sustain modest growth in 1997, analysts said. During the past year, the dollar's strength in key markets such as Japan and Germany as well as modest, sometimes negative, sales growth, dragged down several key stocks, particularly the sector's powerhouse, Procter and Gamble. Page 13.
